from pysat.solvers import Glucose3
import itertools

n = 22
solver = Glucose3()

# Variables: edge (i, j) for 0 <= i < j < n
# Map (i, j) to 1 .. n*(n-1)//2
def var(i, j):
    if i > j:
        i, j = j, i
    # i from 0 to n-2
    # j from i+1 to n-1
    # index = i * n - i*(i+1)//2 + j - i - 1 + 1
    idx = i * n - i * (i + 1) // 2 + j - i
    return idx

# No red K_4 (red is 0, so not all 0 -> at least one 1 -> at least one var is True)
for clique in itertools.combinations(range(n), 4):
    clause = [var(i, j) for i, j in itertools.combinations(clique, 2)]
    solver.add_clause(clause)

# No blue K_5 (blue is 1, so not all 1 -> at least one 0 -> at least one var is False)
for clique in itertools.combinations(range(n), 5):
    clause = [-var(i, j) for i, j in itertools.combinations(clique, 2)]
    solver.add_clause(clause)

print("Solving...")
if solver.solve():
    print("SAT")
    model = solver.get_model()
    # Extract colors
    colors = []
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            v = var(i, j)
            colors.append(1 if model[v - 1] > 0 else 0)
    print(colors)
else:
    print("UNSAT")
